content.title: About
content.content: Pineapple upside-down cake is a classic American dessert in which caramelized pineapple rings and cherries are placed at the bottom of the pan, then a vanilla batter is poured over them. After baking, the cake is inverted so the fruit “crust” becomes the top layer, giving the dessert a bright aroma and juicy flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cake first appeared in the United States in the early 1920s and quickly became popular because of its simplicity.
Traditional recipes use canned pineapple, but many bakers prefer fresh pineapple lightly sautéed with brown sugar.
The original version used cherry jam instead of fresh cherries, adding extra sweetness.
It is often served chilled, sometimes with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
In Japan a variation exists that adds kiwi slices instead of cherries.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Pineapple is rich in vitamin C, which supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Bromelain
items.content: The enzyme bromelain found in pineapple helps digestion and has anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Dietary Fiber
items.content: The fruit and whole‑grain batter provide dietary fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Energy Boost
items.content: The cake supplies carbohydrates that quickly replenish energy stores.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It contains potassium and magnesium, important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: High Sugar Content
items.content: The cake contains a considerable amount of sugar, so people with diabetes should limit their portion.

items.title: Pineapple Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pineapple, ranging from swelling to itching.

items.title: Caloric Density
items.content: Rich in butter and sugar, the cake is calorie‑dense; moderation is key for weight management.

items.title: Trans Fat
items.content: Using margarine instead of butter can introduce trans fats, which are undesirable for cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the cake in individual slices at room temperature. It can be topped with whipped cream, ice cream, or a dusting of cinnamon. For a fresher taste, add a few slices of fresh pineapple on top.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cake in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. For longer storage, freeze individual portions in a freezer‑safe bag – they retain flavor for up to 2 months. Allow the cake to come to room temperature before serving.
